prompt: For a materially different sanitized system supplied by a qualified reviewer, design and defend a complete failure-containment and recovery contract. Do not use the lesson fixture or model answers, and do not send traffic or change any real policy without explicit separate authorization.
deliverables: User journey, correctness objective, side effects, failure domains, dependencies and explicit exclusions.
End-to-end absolute deadline with queue, service, dependency, response and guard allocations plus cancellation behavior.
Original-operation and attempt model with maximum layered amplification and measured attempt ratio.
Failure-class matrix covering before-send, after-send unknown, timeout, reset, overload, permanent, conflict and cancellation cases.
One retry owner with total budget, attempt cap, exponential backoff, jitter, remaining-deadline and overload stop rules.
Idempotency state machine with principal scope, canonical fingerprint, atomic claim, fencing or lease, durable result, conflict, expiry and reconciliation.
Circuit-breaker design with scope, rolling population, minimum sample, thresholds, open interval, half-open probes, fallback and manual-control risk.
Bulkhead, rate, concurrency and connection limits with critical reserves, tenant or priority fairness and controlled borrowing.
Bounded queue design covering arrival, departure, depth, oldest age, memory, expiry, redrive and recovery drain.
Admission, load-shedding and graceful-degradation contract with approved priority and explicit valid output.
Observability design correlating operations, attempts, deadlines, retry reasons, states, rejects, goodput and recovery.
Authorized fault-test and rollout plan with baseline, cohort, abort, rollback, communications, reconciliation, cleanup and proof limits.
evidenceRequirements: Sanitized input provenance, timestamp, units, populations, topology and known gaps.
Arithmetic showing all timeout allocations fit one deadline and all retry layers fit one total budget.
At least two idempotency crash points and a conflicting-payload test with observed side-effect count.
A same-window comparison demonstrating whether critical work remains protected when another lane saturates.
Circuit evidence with sufficient sample size, open rejection, limited probes and stable recovery or justified continued open state.
Queue evidence including oldest age and expired-work behavior, not depth alone.
Reviewer-observed cleanup and proof that no unapproved target, data, credential, paid resource or policy changed.
Delayed reassessment on a second unseen system with different side-effect and workload semantics.

rubric.observableEvidence: Defines user intention, success, unknown outcome, side effects and exclusions.
Uses one coherent budget, per-hop arithmetic, guard and cancellation semantics.
Distinguishes transport phase, overload, permanent, semantic and unknown outcomes.
Calculates layered attempts and enforces one owner, global budget, backoff, jitter and stop rules.
Shows scoped key, fingerprint, atomicity, lifecycle, conflict, retention and crash recovery.
Defines scope, population, threshold, interval, probes, fallback and convergence.
Reserves critical capacity, bounds borrowing and measures isolation and fairness.
Bounds age, count and memory and defines admission, shedding, degradation and drain.
Correlates user operations, attempts, budgets, policy states, reasons, goodput and correctness.
Uses authority, bounded cohort, baseline, abort, rollback, paced recovery, reconciliation and cleanup.
Addresses abuse, secrets, cardinality, fallback capacity, retention and cost per useful operation.
States alternatives, falsifiers, assumptions, external-validity limits and review triggers.
